newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-United News to merge printing plants.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-United News to merge printing plants.

text.p: British media company United News & Media Plc on Tuesday said its United Newspapers subsidiary would merge its two main printing plants and take an exceptional charge of 32 million pounds ($49.72 million).

The move will merge the two main printing plants serving Express Newspaper Plc, publisher of the Daily Express and Sunday Express tabloid newspapers, and United Provincial Newspapers in the north of England.

The 32 million pound charge reflects the total cost of merging the printing plants along with the previously announced costs to be incurred in reorganising the Express Newspapers publishing activities and related matters. The charge will be taken agaisnt operating profit by United in its full year.
United News said it expects the pay back on the 32 million one-off cost will be achieved over the next three years.
Under the planned printing plant merger, presses currently located at Express Printers in Manchester will be transferred to the United Provincial site at Broughton near Preston.

The merger will take about two years to complete, with the first moves expected to occur early in 1997. The changes will create a significant number of new jobs at Preston but will result in redundancies at Manchester, the company said.
United News said it is hoped that many employees now at Manchester will accept job offers at the Broughton plant.

"I very much regret the necessity of closing our Manchester printing operation, but it is clear that the urban Manchester site limits the opportunities for further enhancements of our newspapers," Stephen Grabiner, chief executive of United Newspapers, said in a statement.

Express Newspapers last week said it was reorganising its Daily and Sunday Express titles, involving 85 job cuts and a 10 million pound investment to improve the quality of the newspapers. The company said the estimated 85 job losses was expected to cost about six million pounds.
Shares of United News & Media closed 1/2 pence lower at 704-1/2 pence.
